answer: In a market for sparrow counts, each account gets a vote only after an auditor chosen after submission verifies a fresh sensor record. A public mirror lists the records by sensor serial and collection window, so two accounts cannot claim the same recording. Every voting vertex must also lock 20 credits that it loses if its record fails the audit. A farm seeking 100 votes must supply 100 separate verified recordings and put 2,000 credits at risk.
